title: Adani Ports lines up MUFG-led bridge loan and up to US$1.45bn equity to fund EUR2.56bn Evos acquisition
summary: Bloomberg reported (12 Nov 2026) that Adani Group plans to fund APSEZ's EUR2.56bn (c. US$2.9bn) acquisition of Dutch liquid-storage operator Evos B.V. with an equity infusion of up to US$1.45bn (about half the price) and a syndicated bridge loan of roughly 18 months, sole-underwritten by MUFG (committed up to EUR2.8bn), with DBS, First Abu Dhabi Bank, Barclays and State Bank of India in talks to join; about EUR1.3bn of existing Evos debt will also be refinanced. Terms are not final. The structure shows APSEZ shifting borrowings into cheaper euro debt (Evos funding cost c.4.5% vs 6.4-6.6% for APSEZ) as it builds its first European terminal platform (eight terminals, 6.3m cbm) - a direct move into DP World's European and liquid-bulk territory.
location: Netherlands / Germany / Spain / Belgium / Malta (Evos terminals)

title: Gulftainer seeks consultants for Al Dhaid multimodal logistics hub (feasibility, masterplan, engineering)
summary: MEED reported (19 Nov 2026) that Gulftainer is seeking consultants for feasibility, masterplanning, connectivity and detailed engineering services for its planned multimodal logistics hub at Al Dhaid, Sharjah. This moves the 150-hectare 'Al Dhaid Multi-Modal Trade Corridor' (announced June 2026 as a PPP with Sharjah Ports Authority; inland container yard, CFS and Etihad Rail integration with 1.5m TEU/yr inland capacity, c.50 km from Khorfakkan) from concept into procurement. Alongside the 1,000-truck fleet and KAFEZ investments announced in early November, it underpins Gulftainer's bid to make Khorfakkan a landbridge gateway to the Gulf that competes directly with DP World's Jebel Ali and east-coast plans.

title: Boskalis-led JV selected for SEK 2.3bn Gothenburg (Skandia Gateway) fairway deepening
summary: The Swedish Maritime Administration selected a joint venture of Boskalis Sweden, Van Oord Sweden and Rohde Nielsen for the Skandia Gateway fairway deepening at the Port of Gothenburg, one of Sweden's largest dredging projects. The base assignment is worth about SEK 2.3bn (c. USD 228m) with further work possible under options; scope covers c. 7 million m3 of loose material and rock to raise maximum draught from 13.5 m to 16.5 m (option to 17.5 m), plus fairway marking adjustments. Contract signing is planned for end-2026 if the award is not challenged, with works from August 2027 to autumn 2028. Boskalis' share of the JV value was not disclosed; the award follows the Boskalis/Van Oord Lulea contract earlier in 2026 and consolidates Boskalis' position in Nordic port-infrastructure dredging.
capacity: c. 7 million m3 dredging; draught 13.5 m to 16.5 m

title: Boskalis wins long-term Apache North Sea subsea decommissioning contract for Forties and Beryl fields
summary: Boskalis secured a long-term contract from Apache North Sea, following a competitive tender, for a subsea decommissioning programme across the Forties and Beryl areas of the UK North Sea. Scope covers flushing, disconnection, recovery and disposal of subsea wells, structures, pipelines and associated infrastructure, using a predominantly ROV-led approach and Boskalis' recently expanded offshore fleet. Contract value and duration were not disclosed. The award extends Boskalis' offshore energy/decommissioning franchise, an adjacent market to the offshore marine services offered by P&O Maritime.
location: UK North Sea (Forties and Beryl fields)

title: Cochin Shipyard signs Rs 498.58 crore MoD contract for refit and re-powering of frigate INS Betwa
summary: India's Ministry of Defence signed a contract worth over Rs 498 crore (c. USD 56m) with Cochin Shipyard Ltd in New Delhi on 11 November 2026 for the normal refit and re-powering of INS Betwa, a Brahmaputra-class frigate. The project replaces the ship's steam propulsion with a diesel-engine plant and installs a modernised weapon suite, and is expected to involve more than 50 MSMEs. The win adds to CSL's fast-growing ship repair book (ship repair revenue up c. 30% YoY in Q2 FY27) and reinforces its position as India's leading naval refit yard, relevant to Drydocks World's planned ISRF Kochi JV with CSL.

title: Cochin Shipyard and Damen sign MoU on specialised and low-emission vessel building in India
summary: At the India Shipbuilding Investment Conclave 2026 in New Delhi (Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways), Cochin Shipyard CMD Jose VJ and Damen Shipyards Group regional sales director (Asia) Dingeman van Woerden signed an MoU to explore cooperation on specialised vessels, mainly tugs and other advanced/high-tech ships, including hybrid, methanol-capable and electric designs for domestic and export markets. CSL would use Damen designs and propulsion technology, with a focus on localisation, technology cooperation and knowledge sharing; no financial terms or vessel numbers were disclosed. The tie-up builds on CSL's existing electric TRAnsverse tug programme for Svitzer and positions CSL/Damen as a local-content tug supplier in India.
partners: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways (India)

title: Svitzer takes delivery of another TRAnsverse 2900 as newbuild pipeline reaches 27 tugs
summary: Svitzer accepted delivery of the TRAnsverse 2900 tug Svitzer Rast from Cheoy Lee's Hin Lee yard in China, the second TRAnsverse 2900 in a month, both bound for Europe (Svitzer Resolute heading to the UK). Svitzer said it has signed 12 further newbuild contracts since August 2026 and its build pipeline now stands at 27 tugs (22 TRAnsverse, four Damen and one RAmparts 2300SX), with deliveries expected at one to two tugs a month in coming years from its multi-yard network (China, Turkey, Brazil, India). COO Kasper Karlsen said the global yard capacity strategy is now paying dividends in meeting customer demand; the scale of the programme underlines Svitzer's fleet-renewal lead over P&O Maritime in harbour and terminal towage.
location: Global (delivery from Hin Lee shipyard, China)

title: Maersk inaugurates 16,000 sqm bonded Semarang Consolidation Centre in Central Java
summary: Maersk inaugurated a new consolidation centre in Semarang, Central Java (Indonesia) on 11 November 2026: 16,000+ sqm, 15,800 CBM capacity and 11,300 pallet positions on six-level racking, operating under a Pusat Logistik Berikat (PLB) bonded-logistics licence. The site sits 4 km from Tanjung Emas port and 0.3 km from Maersk's container depot, and bundles warehousing/consolidation with depot services, road/rail inland transport and Maersk's ocean network for footwear, garment and furniture exporters. It extends Maersk's Indonesian footprint to over 128,000 sqm of warehousing across 15 sites; investment value not disclosed. Relevant to DP World Logistics' own Indonesia/SE Asia integrated-logistics ambitions.

title: DHL Supply Chain opens first Cebu warehouse, a 5,000 sqm built-to-suit site for Teradyne
summary: DHL Supply Chain announced (press release 11 November 2026) the opening of its first warehouse in Cebu, Philippines: a 5,000 sqm built-to-suit facility in a PEZA economic zone in Lapu-Lapu City dedicated to semiconductor test-equipment maker Teradyne, which opened on 30 October 2026. DHL handles inbound receiving, pallet/carton/crate picking, dispatch and shuttle transport to Teradyne's plant, with temperature-controlled storage and a shared real-time inventory dashboard. Investment value not disclosed. Illustrates DHL's push into dedicated electronics/semiconductor contract logistics inside Asian economic zones, a segment DP World Logistics also targets.

title: DHL Global Forwarding launches first dedicated India freighter: twice-weekly Hong Kong–Navi Mumbai–Liège B747F
summary: On 16 November 2026 DHL Global Forwarding announced a new dedicated twice-weekly Boeing 747 freighter rotation linking Hong Kong, Navi Mumbai (NMI) and Liège, operated via DHL Aviation as airline supplier. The aircraft offers ~100 t per flight, with an initial 25-30 t per flight (50-60 t/week) targeted on the India sectors for life sciences, electronics, engineering and advanced-manufacturing cargo, connecting into DHL's European road network from Liège. It is DGF's first dedicated flight serving India, and a Bengaluru-Europe service is planned for March 2027. Strengthens DHL's controlled air-freight capacity on the India-Europe lane where DP World has no comparable air-forwarding product.
capacity: Boeing 747F, ~100 t/flight, twice weekly; 25-30 t/flight on India sectors

title: DHL Supply Chain reports 12% Q3 2026 revenue growth; 2026 contract wins (TCV) to exceed EUR 8bn
summary: DHL Group's contract-logistics division DHL Supply Chain issued a growth update on 17 November 2026 reporting Q3 2026 revenue up 12.0% year on year (Americas +13.1%, EMEA +11.7%, Asia Pacific +9.9%), driven by life sciences & healthcare, technology/data centres, retail, consumer, new energy and automotive. Total contract value signed in 2026 is expected to far exceed EUR 8bn (about USD 9.3bn), backed by a qualified pipeline of over EUR 36bn, with ~90% contract renewal rate across 55+ countries and 250+ pharma warehouses. Investment priorities named are AI/robotics, automation, acquisitions, LatAm/US healthcare capacity and battery logistics. Confirms the scale gap between the world's largest contract-logistics provider and DP World Logistics.
